programs.haiku:
"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2945 -- the " line" token of a Python stack trace.

A Python traceback names a source file and then a line number:

    File "/path/to/module.py", line 42, in f

This component responds to the word " line" that comes right after the closing quote and
comma of such a file name. There it is strongly negative: about -23 when the file is a real
source file (its name ends in .py), and about -8 when the frame is interactive code
(`File "<stdin>", line 1` or `File "<string>", line 1`). Everywhere else it is near zero,
so the program predicts 0 at every other token.

The program is stateless: it looks only at the current token and the three before it.
"""

READS = ()

SOURCE_FILE_LINE = -23.0  # " line" after ...something.py",
INTERACTIVE_LINE = -8.0  # " line" after "<stdin>", or "<string>",


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    if len(tokens) < 4 or tokens[-1] != " line":
        return carry, 0.0
    quoted_name = "".join(tokens[-4:-1])  # e.g. 'utils.py",' or '<stdin>",'
    if quoted_name.endswith('.py",'):
        return carry, SOURCE_FILE_LINE
    if quoted_name.endswith('>",'):
        return carry, INTERACTIVE_LINE
    return carry, 0.0

programs.sol:
"""Approximate a response to detached formatting and encoding artifacts.

Add fixed scores for whitespace, brackets, separator lines, literal escapes,
and fragmented or unusual Unicode. Ordinary words usually get only the
near-zero baseline. Recent text supplies boundary and escape context; this
is not a reconstruction of the component's ordinary lexical variation.
"""
import re
import unicodedata as ud

READS = ()
TEXT_COMMAND = r'\\(?:text|mbox|box|mathrm|textrm|textbf)$'


def whitespace(s, previous, tail):
    if not s.isspace():
        return 0.0
    n = s.count(' ')
    newline = previous.endswith('\n')
    end = previous.rstrip()
    if '\xa0' in s:
        score = 0.09 + 0.09 * (len(s) > 1) + 0.76 * newline
    elif '\n' in s:
        score = -0.01 + 0.17 * (n >= 3)
    elif '\t' in s:
        score = -0.01
    elif n:
        score = 0.05 - 0.07 * (n >= 3 and n % 4 == 3)
        score += 0.21 * (n >= 4 and n % 4 == 0)
    else:
        score = 0.20
    score += 0.43 * (previous.isspace() and '\xa0' in previous)
    score += 0.46 * end.endswith(('•', '–', '—', '▪', '●'))
    score += 0.23 * end.endswith(('.', '?', '!'))
    score += 0.04 * end.endswith((':', ',', ';'))
    score += 0.13 * end.endswith(('>', '|', '[', '-', '*', '#'))
    score += 0.12 * (newline and ' ' in previous)
    if previous.endswith('.') and len(tail) > 1 and tail[-2].isalpha():
        score -= 0.11
    return score


def marks(s, previous):
    mark = s.strip()
    if not mark or any(c.isalnum() for c in mark):
        return 0.0
    score = 0.0
    boundary = previous.rstrip().endswith(('.', '?', '!'))
    if mark[0] in '([{':
        score += 0.11 * (mark[0] == '[')
        score += 0.22 * previous.isspace()
        score += 0.07 * previous.rstrip().endswith((',', ':', ';', ')'))
        score += 0.37 * boundary + 0.08 * previous.endswith('\n')
        if len(mark) > 1 and mark[1] in '\"\'':
            score -= 0.15
    elif mark[0] in ')]}' and any(c in '([{' for c in mark[1:]):
        score += 0.15
    score += 0.14 * (len(mark) >= 4 and len(set(mark)) == 1)
    if '\n' in s and mark in ('+', '-', '<', '>', '|', '~', '*'):
        score += 0.07 + 0.53 * (previous.strip() == mark)
    if boundary and not any(c in '([{' for c in mark):
        score += 0.19
    return score


def encoding(s, b, raw_tail):
    if '\ufffd' not in s:
        return 0.4 if s.strip() and ud.category(s.strip()[0]) == 'Cf' else 0.0
    # UTF-8 fragments beginning Latin-1, punctuation, or private-use glyphs.
    lead = b.lstrip(b' ')
    score = 0.85 * lead.startswith(b'\xc2')
    score += 0.52 * lead.startswith(b'\xe2\x80')
    score -= 0.18 * lead.startswith(b'\xee')
    raw = raw_tail + b
    text = raw.decode('utf8', 'ignore')
    category = ud.category(text[-1]) if text else ''
    pending = re.search(b'[\xc2-\xf4][\x80-\xbf]{0,2}$', raw)
    pending = pending.group() if pending else b''
    score += 0.72 * (pending.startswith(b'\xee') or category == 'Co')
    score += 0.10 * (pending.startswith(b'\xe2\x81') or category in ('Cf', 'Zs'))
    score += 0.31 * bool(text and 128 <= ord(text[-1]) <= 159)
    score += 0.23 * (category == 'Sc')
    return score


def escapes(s, previous, tail):
    word = s.strip()
    score = 0.0
    if word.startswith('\\'):
        score += 0.05
        score += 0.26 * (previous.isspace() or previous.startswith('\\'))
        if word.startswith('\\x'):
            score += 0.64 - 0.37 * (len(word) > 2)
        if word in ('\\n', '\\r'):
            score += -0.04 + 0.28 * tail.endswith(('\\n', '\\r'))
            score -= 0.12 * previous.startswith(' ')
        score -= 0.04 * ('"' in word or "'" in word)
    if re.search(TEXT_COMMAND, tail + s):
        score += 0.77
    if tail.endswith('\\') and re.fullmatch(r'x[0-9a-fA-F]*', word):
        score += 0.77
    if word.startswith('{') and re.search(TEXT_COMMAND, tail):
        score += 0.86
    if re.search(r'\\x[0-9a-fA-F]?$', tail) and re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-fA-F]+', s):
        score += 0.25
    return score


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous, tail, raw_tail = '', '', b''
    else:
        _, previous, tail, raw_tail = carry
    s, b = prefix.token_strings[-1], prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    value = 0.001 + whitespace(s, previous, tail) + marks(s, previous)
    value += encoding(s, b, raw_tail) + escapes(s, previous, tail)
    if not previous and s == '\t':
        value -= 0.77
    if s == '0' and previous.rstrip().endswith(('[', '(')):
        value += 0.17
    return (doc, s, (tail + s)[-40:], (raw_tail + b)[-12:]), float(value)

"""Layer-1 MLP component 2947: a "symbol break" detector.

What it responds to, in plain terms: ordinary prose words leave it at about zero, and
so does punctuation inside words. It switches on for the symbol-like tokens that break
up running text: a bare space after punctuation or a bullet, non-breaking spaces,
indentation, backslash escapes such as \\x, opening brackets and LaTeX braces, and
lone UTF-8 byte fragments (which decode alone to U+FFFD). How strongly it fires depends
on what came just before: a symbol after another symbol (an nbsp after an nbsp, an escape
after an escape, a space after punctuation) fires hardest; a space or indent that follows
an ordinary word is slightly negative.

How the program works: each token is put into one of about eleven kinds by its text
(byte, nbsp, indent, space, newline, punct, open, escape, bullet, word, other). The
previous token is put into a class (word, symbol, or other). The prediction is the mean
activation for that (kind, previous class) cell, and for a few (kind, previous kind)
pairs that differ strongly from it, taken from the training rows. The tables below are
those means, rounded.
"""

READS = ()

SYMBOL_KINDS = {"byte", "nbsp", "indent", "newline", "escape", "open", "bullet", "punct", "space"}

# value by (current kind) -> {previous token class: mean activation}
CLASS_TABLE = {
    "nbsp": {"word": -0.02, "sym": 0.50, "other": -0.07},
    "escape": {"word": 0.08, "sym": 0.21, "other": -0.03},
    "byte": {"word": 0.06, "sym": 0.12, "other": 0.02},
    "bullet": {"word": 0.03, "sym": 0.14, "other": -0.05},
    "open": {"word": 0.03, "sym": 0.21, "other": 0.02},
    "indent": {"word": -0.02, "sym": 0.09, "other": -0.11},
    "space": {"word": -0.03, "sym": 0.13, "other": -0.03},
    "newline": {"word": -0.01, "sym": 0.14, "other": -0.01},
    "punct": {"word": -0.01, "sym": 0.09, "other": -0.01},
    "other": {"word": -0.00, "sym": 0.02, "other": 0.00},
    "word": {"word": 0.00, "sym": 0.01, "other": -0.00},
}

# exact (current kind, previous kind) pairs that differ strongly from the table
PAIR_TABLE = {
    ("space", "indent"): 0.00,
    ("newline", "newline"): 0.40,
    ("indent", "newline"): 0.19,
    ("punct", "indent"): 0.01,
    ("escape", "punct"): 0.10,
    ("space", "bullet"): 0.44,
    ("newline", "nbsp"): 0.86,
    ("space", "punct"): 0.18,
    ("space", "open"): 0.41,
    ("escape", "escape"): 0.34,
    ("word", "escape"): 0.07,
    ("indent", "punct"): 0.04,
    ("nbsp", "space"): 0.14,
    ("space", "nbsp"): 0.55,
    ("indent", "indent"): 0.23,
    ("newline", "punct"): 0.08,
}


def kind(s):
    """A short class for one token, from its text alone (s is the token decoded alone)."""
    if "\ufffd" in s:
        return "byte"
    if s == "":
        return "other"
    body = s.strip()
    if body == "":
        if "\xa0" in s:
            return "nbsp"
        if s == " ":
            return "space"
        if "\n" in s or "\r" in s:
            return "newline"
        return "indent"
    if body.isalnum():
        return "word"
    if body.startswith("\\"):
        return "escape"
    if body in {"[", "(", "{", "](", "[@", "][", "{}", "$$", "$\\", "&#"}:
        return "open"
    if body in {"•", "·", "··", "–", "*"}:
        return "bullet"
    if all(not c.isalnum() for c in body):
        return "punct"
    return "other"


def prev_class(kind_name):
    if kind_name == "word":
        return "word"
    if kind_name in SYMBOL_KINDS:
        return "sym"
    return "other"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at this position, from the current token and the one before it."""
    cur = kind(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    value = CLASS_TABLE[cur][prev_class("other")]
    if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        prev = kind(prefix.token_strings[-2])
        value = CLASS_TABLE[cur][prev_class(prev)]
        value = PAIR_TABLE.get((cur, prev), value)
    return carry, float(value)

programs.sol:
"""Recognize permission, eligibility, legal status and classification language.

English word-family rules give mostly negative values. Phrase rules emphasize
formal classification and entitlement; a fading trace carries this topic into
nearby connectives. Chinese eligibility and permission terms are recognized
through dictionary glosses. State resets at document boundaries. Openings are
mildly positive, except the strongly negative colon in an initial 'Title:'.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import re
import regex
import cedict

READS = ()

# Word-family pattern, activation, whether it establishes a formal/legal topic.
RULES = (
    (r'eligib', -1.50, True),
    (r'exempt', -1.06, True),
    (r'deduct', -1.64, True),
    (r'taxed$|taxable$|taxation$', -1.19, True),
    (r'tax(es)?$', -0.43, True),
    (r'citizenship$', -1.05, True),
    (r'allowed$|granted$', -0.78, True),
    (r'considered$', -0.66, False),
    (r'insur|compens|allowance|reimburs', -0.58, True),
    (r'allow|permit|permiss|forbid|prohibit', -0.33, True),
    (r'entitl|qualify|qualifies$', -0.50, True),
    (r'recogni[sz]|classif|deemed$|counted$', -0.45, False),
    (r'laws?$|legal|lawful|statut|jurisdict', -0.45, True),
    (r'offen[cs]|convict|penalt|liab|presumpt', -0.63, True),
    (r'requirement|prerequis|mandatory$|obligat', -0.54, True),
    (r'requir|oblig', -0.21, True),
    (r'certif|regist|licensure$', -0.33, True),
    (r'claim|rights$', -0.38, True),
    (r'apply|applies$|applicable$|filing$', -0.27, True),
    (r'maximum$|minimum$|restrict|valid', -0.19, True),
    (r'immigr|visas?$', -1.12, True),
    (r'entity$|entities$|status$|subsect|purposes$', -0.36, True),
    (r'free$', -0.26, False),
)
SMALL_WORDS = {
    'all': .08, 'each': .08, 'many': .08, 'some': .08, 'only': .08,
    'less': .08, 'fewer': .08, 'shall': .22, 'under': -.37,
    'as': -.10, 'for': -.05, 'if': -.03, 'unless': -.03, 'when': -.03,
}
CONNECTIVES = {'as': -.49, 'for': -.38, 'to': -.15, 'under': -.72,
               'of': -.13, 'a': -.28, 'an': -.17, 'from': -.33, 'if': -.34}
CLASSIFYING = set(('recognized regarded classified defined deemed counted '
    'treated designated marked identified named termed billed certified '
    'qualify qualifies recorded cited used recognize regard classify define '
    'deem count treat designate mark identify name term bill certify record '
    'cite use').split())
ENTITLEMENT = set('entitle entitled entitlement entitlements qualify qualifies '
                  'right rights'.split())
QUALIFYING = set(('eligible liable responsible apply applying requirement '
    'requirements prerequisite prerequisites mandatory obligation obligations '
    'insurance compensation allowance allowances reimbursement reimbursements '
    'exempt exempted exemption exemptions deadline exception criteria coverage '
    'connection admission license').split()) | ENTITLEMENT

# Dictionary gloss patterns, not a list of Chinese model tokens.
GLOSSES = (
    (r'eligib|qualific|prerequisite', -.81),
    (r'free.*charge', -.33),
    (r'to permit|to allow|to require|requirement|to apply for|cannot|must not', -.12),
    (r'legal|lawful|citizenship|\blaw\b|regulation|certificat|licen|insurance|'
     r'to pay a fee', -.15),
)

@lru_cache(maxsize=16384)
def word_family(word):
    for pattern, value, topic in RULES:
        if re.match(pattern, word):
            return value, topic
    return SMALL_WORDS.get(word, 0.0), False

@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def translations(word):
    if not regex.search(r'\p{Script=Han}', word):
        return frozenset()
    gloss = '; '.join(cedict.glosses(word)).lower()
    return frozenset(i for i, (pattern, _) in enumerate(GLOSSES)
                     if re.search(pattern, gloss))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc, text = prefix.document_ids[-1], prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous, tail, topic, position = '', '', 0.0, 0
    else:
        _, previous, tail, topic, position = carry
        position += 1
    word = text.strip().lower()
    boundary = position == 0 or text[:1].isspace() or not tail[-1:].isalpha()
    if not boundary and word.isascii() and word.isalpha() and previous.isalpha():
        word = previous + word
    strength, formal = word_family(word)
    translated = set()
    if position == 0:
        value = .21
    else:
        translated.update(translations(word))
        if len(word) == 1 and regex.search(r'\p{Script=Han}', word):
            translated.update(translations((tail + word)[-2:]))
        value = -.0022 + strength + sum(GLOSSES[i][1] for i in translated)
        if boundary:
            value += CONNECTIVES.get(word, 0.0) * topic
        if word == 'as' and boundary:
            if previous in CLASSIFYING:
                value -= .61
            if previous in {'recognized', 'marked', 'counted', 'accepted',
                            'qualifies', 'certification'}:
                value -= 1.05
        if word == 'to' and boundary and previous in ENTITLEMENT:
            value -= .66
        if word == 'to' and previous in {'entitled', 'entitlement'}:
            value -= .32
        if word == 'for' and boundary and previous in QUALIFYING:
            value -= .32
        if word == 'under' and previous in {
                'covered', 'protected', 'exempt', 'exemption'}:
            value -= 1.36
        if word == 'v' and tail.strip()[:1].isupper():
            value -= .34  # Legal case citation: Name v. Name.
        if word == '§':
            value -= .37
        if word in {'deduction', 'deductible'} and previous == 'tax':
            value -= 1.02
        if previous in {'be', 'is', 'are', 'was', 'were', 'been'} and word in {
                'considered', 'allowed', 'exempt', 'taxed', 'eligible',
                'liable', 'permitted'}:
            value -= .72
    if position == 1 and tail == 'Title' and text == ':':
        value -= 7.80
    topic = max(topic * .8, float(formal or bool(translated)))
    return (doc, word, text, topic, position), value

"""Legal, tax and eligibility vocabulary, pushed negative.

Most of this component's activation is near zero. It goes clearly negative on words about
who may or may not do or get something: eligibility and entitlement, legal and tax status,
citizenship, offences, exemptions, requirements. The strongest values are on the word itself
("eligible", "considered", "citizenship", "allowed", "exempt", "deduction"). The short
words that follow such language are pushed negative as well, each in its own way: "as"
after a verb of classing something ("defined as", "treated as", "recognized as"), "for" after
an application or criteria word ("apply for", "eligible for"), "to" after an entitlement or
right ("entitled to", "right to"), and "under" in general. Words that fade through a passage
of legal text drag the small function words after them negative too; this is tracked with
a running, fading count of legal words. The first token of each document is pushed slightly
positive. Everything else predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

CATEGORIES = [
    # who is eligible, allowed, considered, a citizen, or exempt; offences
    ([
        "considered", "citizenship", "allowed", "eligible", "eligibility", "ineligible",
        "exempt", "exemption", "deduction", "deductible", "deductions", "presumption", "visa",
        "legally", "liable", "liability", "taxable", "taxed", "taxation", "barred",
        "lawful", "prohibited", "offense", "felony", "misdemeanor", "manslaughter",
        "statute", "subsection", "§", "§§",
    ], -1.2),
    # legal and tax status, rights, claims, requirements, insurance
    ([
        "legal", "law", "laws", "tax", "taxes", "federal", "claim", "claims", "rights",
        "entitled", "entitlement", "requirement", "requirements", "entity", "registration",
        "registered", "insurance", "coverage", "compensation", "granted", "permitted",
        "allow", "allows", "qualify", "qualifies", "restrictions", "charged", "conviction",
        "penalty", "recognized", "allowance", "scholarship", "status", "classification",
        "certified", "court", "circuit", "proceedings", "obligations", "administrative",
        "medicaid", "medicare", "benefits", "mandatory", "permit", "residency",
    ], -0.5),
    # requirements and conditions, weaker
    ([
        "required", "require", "requires", "subject", "apply", "applicable", "prove",
        "documents", "valid", "validity", "accepted", "approved", "covered",
    ], -0.25),
    # money and "free of charge"
    (["free", "pay", "fee", "fees", "days"], -0.25),
    # the same legal and tax ideas in other languages
    (["条件", "申请", "要求", "税", "税金", "免费", "無料", "免費", "身份证", "貸款", "налог",
      "налогов", "граждан", "право", "документов", "注册", "登记", "法律", "合法", "手続き",
      "자격", "무료", "droit", "deben"], -0.3),
    # jurisdictions, as in "under Canadian law" or "in Virginia"
    (["canada", "india", "france", "england", "virginia", "florida", "california",
      "illinois", "maryland", "pennsylvania", "massachusetts", "oregon", "maine", "michigan",
      "ohio", "texas", "germany", "australia", "ontario", "scotland", "wales"], -0.25),
]

# The small word after a legal word, by what came before it.
AFTER = {
    "as": (-1.0, {"defined", "treated", "recognized", "identified", "considered", "regarded",
                  "used", "described", "counted", "calculated", "recorded", "served",
                  "interpreted", "expressed", "shown", "classified"}),
    "for": (-0.8, {"apply", "applied", "applying", "application", "eligible", "eligibility",
                   "award", "criteria", "rate", "rates", "conditions", "required", "connection",
                   "qualify", "qualifies", "requirement", "requirements"}),
    "to": (-0.6, {"entitled", "entitlement", "right", "rights", "subject", "authority",
                  "allowed", "allow", "apply", "applies", "required", "permitted"}),
}
UNDER_VALUE = -0.45
CONTEXT = {"as", "for", "to", "under", "if", "must", "can", "of", "by", "from", "in", "on"}
CONTEXT_VALUE = -0.15
FADE = 0.8
DOC_START = 0.2

VALUE = {}
for words, value in CATEGORIES:
    for word in words:
        VALUE[word] = value


def word(token):
    return token.strip().lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (fading count of legal words so far, value of the previous token).
    current = word(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    if len(prefix.token_strings) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return (0.0, 0.0), DOC_START
    legal, previous = carry
    legal = FADE * legal + (1.0 if previous <= -0.4 else 0.0)
    value = VALUE.get(current, 0.0)
    before = word(prefix.token_strings[-2])
    if current in AFTER and before in AFTER[current][1]:
        out = AFTER[current][0]
    elif current == "under":
        out = UNDER_VALUE
    elif current in CONTEXT:
        out = CONTEXT_VALUE * legal
    else:
        out = value
    return (legal, value), out

"""Document-start detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2950.

The component is silent almost everywhere (activation std about 0.1) except on the first
token of each document, i.e. the token right after <|endoftext|> (or the first token of a
row). There it fires strongly, and how strongly depends on what kind of token it is:
chat markers most, ordinary words next, punctuation and whitespace less, and digits barely
at all. At a document's first token the model's attention sees only that token, so its
activation is a fixed function of the token itself, and the kinds below capture most of it.
"""

READS = ()

# Typical activation at a document's first token, by kind of token.
START_VALUES = {
    "chat_marker": 11.6,  # <|im_start|>, <|im_end|>, ...
    "word_space": 9.7,  # a word with a leading space: " the", " to", " was"
    "word": 7.5,  # a word without one: "The", "package", "Person"
    "mixed": 8.8,  # letters mixed with digits or symbols: ".com", "ac3"
    "punct": 4.7,  # symbols only: ".", ",", "(", "#", "{"
    "space": 5.0,  # newlines, tabs, indentation
    "digit": 1.6,  # digit strings: "0" to "9"
}


def kind(s):
    """The kind of token a string (one token, decoded alone) is."""
    w = s.strip()
    if s.startswith("<|") and s.endswith("|>"):
        return "chat_marker"
    if not w:
        return "space"
    if w.isdigit():
        return "digit"
    if w.isalpha():
        return "word_space" if s[0] == " " else "word"
    if not any(c.isalnum() for c in w):
        return "punct"
    return "mixed"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token: its kind's typical value if it opens a document
    (it is the row's first token, or the document id changed since the last token), else 0."""
    t = prefix.position
    opens_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not opens_document:
        return None, 0.0
    return None, START_VALUES[kind(prefix.token_strings[-1])]

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 2952: an end-of-turn newline detector.

Main effect: it goes strongly negative (about -0.63) on the newline token that directly
follows a chat-template end-of-turn token `<|im_end|>`.

Minor effect: it is weakly negative (about -0.1) on the first token of each document in a
packed row (the first token of a row, or the first token after `<|endoftext|>`), where the
model's attention restarts.

Everywhere else it predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

END_OF_TURN = "<|im_end|>"
NEWLINE_AFTER_END_OF_TURN = -0.63
DOCUMENT_START = -0.1


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):

    if t > 0 and prefix.token_strings[t] == "\n" and prefix.token_strings[t - 1] == END_OF_TURN:

"""Mid-word fragment detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2953.

The component is sparse: it is nearly silent on most tokens and fires, sometimes
strongly, on pieces of a word that the tokenizer split into several tokens, when the
piece continues a Latin- or Cyrillic-script word (no leading space, the previous token
ends in a letter). This program predicts a small constant on such pieces and 0
elsewhere. Only the continuation pattern is captured; which fragments spike is not.
"""

READS = ()

FRAGMENT_VALUE = 0.02


def _latin_or_cyrillic(ch):
    code = ord(ch)
    return code < 0x250 or 0x400 <= code < 0x530


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, 0.0
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    continues = token[:1].isalpha() and before[-1:].isalpha()
    if continues and _latin_or_cyrillic(token[0]):
        return None, FRAGMENT_VALUE
    return None, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2954 -- a sparse "the digit 5 (and friends)" detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
- Mostly silent. Its activation is near zero on almost every token.
- It fires on the digit "5", most strongly when the 5 is glued to letters, as in
  identifiers such as "hdf5", "perl5", "route53", "f5" (strongest, about 0.8).
  A 5 after a space, as in "GTA 5", is weaker (about 0.3). A 5 that is
  part of a decimal ("2.5", "0.5") is negative (about -0.25).
- It also fires weakly on spelled-out five ("five", "Five", "fifth",
  "fifteen", "五", "十五") (about 0.4), and on the day-of-month digits "0" or
  "1" that follow a "3" in dates such as "September 30" (about 0.5).
- The first token of a row gets a small negative value (-0.12).
- Everything else is 0. The real activation also has a diffuse, unexplained
  spread over common tokens, which this program does not model.

Predictions are in the component's own units (activation = (x.V) * |U|).
"""

FIVE_WORDS = {" five", " Five", "five", "Five", " fifth", "fifth", " fifteen", "fifteen", "五", "十五"}
READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if prefix.position == 0:
        return None, -0.12
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2][-1:]  # last character of the previous token
    if tok == "5":
        if before.isalpha():
            return None, 0.8  # glued to a word: hdf5, perl5, route53
        if before == ".":
            return None, -0.25  # decimal point: 2.5, 0.5
        if before.isdigit():
            return None, 0.1  # inside a number
        return None, 0.3  # after a space or punctuation: "GTA 5"
    if tok in FIVE_WORDS:
        return None, 0.4
    if tok in ("0", "1") and before == "3":
        return None, 0.5  # day of month: "September 30"
    return None, 0.0

What it does: this component fires on the verb (or verb-like word) that introduces a
deliberate action on an object: "use", "using", "used", "add", "put", "set", "try",

introduced it ("I used", "let me set", "we can use", "maybe try"); weaker when the verb

    # other languages
    "使用": 1.0, "用": 0.8, "加": 0.7, "添加": 0.8, "选择": 0.8, "把": 0.5, "将": 0.4,
    "usar": 0.8, "использовать": 0.8,

# Words that introduce the verb: a person, a modal, or an adverb of intention.
CUES = {"i", "we", "you", "me", "let", "maybe", "perhaps", "should", "can", "could", "must",
        "will", "would", "just", "then", "by", "also", "so", "now", "to", "need", "try",
        "simply", "or", "and", "'s", "'ll", "'ve", "'m", "’s", "’ll", "’ve", "’m"}

NEGATIVE = {"help", "want", "wish", "'re", "’re"}

FUNCTION = {"the", "a", "an", "of", "to", "its", "their", "his", "her", "my", "your", "our"}

"""Layer 1 MLP output, component 2956: short all-caps acronym pieces.

What it does
------------
The component fires on the second (or third) piece of an all-caps word that the
tokenizer has split into several glued tokens, such as the "BE" in "C|BE", the
"CU" in "W|CU", the "AS" in "KR|AS", the "CA" in "YM|CA" or the "OD" in "D|OD".
It is the token that completes a short acronym or gene/code name. The activation
is large when the word so far is 1 or 2 letters and the piece brings the word to
3 or 4 letters. It is weaker when the word so far is longer, and near zero for
long pieces.

Rules, in plain terms
---------------------
- Look at the current token. It must be a bare run of capital letters (after
  stripping a leading space).
- A piece that starts with a space begins a new word. A 2- or 3-letter one gets a
  weak value (0.2). A single letter gets nothing.
- A glued piece (no leading space) is a continuation. Count the capital letters
  of the word before it: the glued pieces back to the word's first piece, which
  may carry a leading space, in the same document.
  - No caps before it: 0.15 for a 2- or 3-letter piece, else 0.
  - Piece of 1 or 2 letters, word so far plus piece is 3 letters: 1.0.
  - Same, total is 4 letters: 0.5.
  - Otherwise: 0.
- Everything else (lowercase, digits, punctuation) predicts 0.

The values were read off per-class mean activations on 1024 training rows. They
are close to the best a lookup over these classes can do.

What this leaves out
--------------------
- Within-class variance is large. Whether a given acronym fires strongly depends
  on whether it is a familiar term (UCI, CBE, HRA fire; DDL, TGF in code often do
  not). The program can't tell.
- Lowercase fragments inside identifiers (e.g. the "sc" in "h[sc]70") carry a
  weak signal. Adding them lowered the fit, so they are left out.
- Rare large outliers are not modelled: a single colon after "Title" at about
  -18.8 and the filler run "··" at a constant -1.35. Neither is a general concept.

Main program: `step` returns the component's predicted activation at the last
token, reading only the token text and the document ids before it.
"""

READS = ()


def _is_caps(text):
    """True for a bare run of capital letters, e.g. "BE" or " MA"."""
    core = text.strip()
    return core.isalpha() and core.isupper()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    piece = tokens[-1]
    if not _is_caps(piece):
        return None, 0.0
    n = len(piece.strip())
    if piece.startswith(" "):
        # The first piece of a new word: weak, and only for 2 or 3 letters.
        return None, (0.2 if n in (2, 3) else 0.0)
    # Capital letters of the word written before this glued piece, same document.
    word = 0
    k = len(tokens) - 2
    while k >= 0 and docs[k] == docs[-1] and _is_caps(tokens[k]):
        word += len(tokens[k].strip())
        if tokens[k].startswith(" "):
            break  # reached the word's first piece
        k -= 1
    if word == 0:
        return None, (0.15 if n in (2, 3) else 0.0)
    if n <= 2 and word + n <= 4:
        return None, (1.0 if word + n == 3 else 0.5)
    return None, 0.0

"""Approximate an orthographic onset signal, not a particular topic.

Predict a negative value at document starts and at new title-case tokens.
Recent capitalization, repetition, and sentence-ending punctuation weaken
that signal. Lowercase pieces of a capitalized word have a small negative
tail. Ordinary tokens otherwise stay near zero.
"""
READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    z = s.strip()
    capital = next((c.isupper() for c in z if c.isalpha()), False)
    fresh = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    if fresh:
        distance, previous, word_capital, seen = 999, '', False, set()
    else:
        _, distance, previous, word_capital, seen = carry
    repeated = s in seen
    attached = (s[:1].isalpha() and previous[-1:].isalpha()
                and word_capital)

    if fresh:
        value = -0.42
    elif z.istitle():
        sentence_end = previous.rstrip().endswith(('.', '!', '?'))
        if distance <= 2 and not previous[-1:].isspace():
            value = 0.02 if repeated else -0.04
        elif distance <= 2 and previous[-1:].isspace():
            value = -0.05 if z.isupper() else (-0.10 if sentence_end else -0.25)
        elif sentence_end:
            value = 0.04 if s.startswith(' ') else -0.06
        elif repeated:
            value = -0.08
        else:
            value = -0.13 if z.isupper() else -0.25
    elif attached and s.islower():
        value = -0.06
    else:
        value = 0.008 if distance <= 4 else -0.005

    seen.add(s)
    word_capital = (capital or attached) and s[-1:].isalpha()
    return (doc, 1 if capital else distance + 1, s, word_capital, seen), value

"""Candidate 2: a document opening, or a capitalised word that starts a new
capitalised run, pushes this component negative; everything else is about zero.

What the component does, as far as simple rules show:
  * The first token of each document (right after <|endoftext|>, or the first token
    of a packed row) gives a clear negative value, about -0.4.
  * A capitalised word (" New", " Making", "Vill", " Positive") that follows a
    token which is not capitalised gives a smaller negative value, about -0.09.
  * A capitalised word that continues a capitalised run (" York" in "New York",
    " Means" in "Ways and Means") is about zero.
  * Other tokens are near zero, with noise of about 0.08 that these rules do not capture.
"""

import re

READS = ()

DOC_START = -0.42
CAP_START = -0.09
CAPITALISED = re.compile(r"^ ?[A-Z]")


def _capitalised(text):
    return CAPITALISED.match(text) is not None


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]:
        return carry, DOC_START
    if _capitalised(prefix.token_strings[-1]) and not _capitalised(prefix.token_strings[-2]):
        return carry, CAP_START
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2959 is a document-start component.

It is almost silent everywhere except on the first token of each document (the token right
after an <|endoftext|> boundary, or the first token of a row). There it writes a large
contribution, typically 5 to 11, whose size depends on what the token looks like:

- a bare newline or carriage return: small (about 3)
- other punctuation, symbols, digits or CJK characters: about 5 to 6
- a word that starts with a space: about 7
- a word with no leading space: about 10 to 11 (capitalised words a little more)
- a space-only token: large (about 13), rare

Every other position predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not new_doc:
        return None, 0.0
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = s.strip()
    if not word:
        return None, 3.0 if "\n" in s or "\r" in s else 13.0
    if not any(c.isalnum() for c in s):
        return None, 5.2
    if word.isdigit():
        return None, 6.3
    if not word[0].isalpha():
        return None, 8.0
    if s[0].isspace():
        return None, 7.5
    return None, 10.8

"""What the component does, in plain terms.

It is a markup-syntax detector that runs negative. It is most negative on the opener of an
HTML/XML comment ("<!--", and "<!"), and on the word right after that opener: in the
EMF-generated comments "<!-- begin-user-doc -->" / "<!-- end-user-doc -->" the words
"begin" and "end" get the largest negative values. It is also negative on the token after
a few other openers ("#include", "---", "{%"), and on a standalone less-than sign
(" <", " (<", " '<"). It is mildly positive on the first token of a new document (the token
after <|endoftext|>), and strongly positive on a run of middle dots "··" (leader dots).
Every other token predicts 0, which is close to the component's typical near-zero value."""
import re

READS = ()

COMMENT_OPEN = {"<!--", "<!"}
COMMENT_WORDS = {"begin", "end"}
# value for the token that follows each opener
AFTER_OPENER = {"#include": -0.75, "---": -0.6, "{%": -1.4}
LESS_THAN = re.compile(r"\s*[(`'\"\\\\]*\s*<")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings
    t = prefix.position
    tok = s[-1]
    cur = tok.strip()
    new_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        return carry, 0.15
    prev = s[-2].strip()
    if cur in COMMENT_OPEN:
        return carry, -4.5
    if prev in COMMENT_OPEN and cur in COMMENT_WORDS:
        return carry, -8.0
    if prev in AFTER_OPENER:
        return carry, AFTER_OPENER[prev]
    if tok == "··":
        return carry, 0.8
    if LESS_THAN.fullmatch(tok):
        return carry, -0.25
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2962 -- an algebra-operator detector (negative sign).

What it does: the component goes negative on the symbols of algebraic formulas, the
operators and powers that sit next to a variable or a number (the ^ or ² in x^2, the + in
2x+3, the − in n−1, the / in 1/2, the √ in √2), and on the number or variable right after
them. It is near silent in prose and code. It is roughly twice as strong inside parentheses or
brackets, where a formula is being worked through.

How the program works: each token is given a role (power, root, plus, minus, times, digit,
variable, bracket, other) and the token before it is given the role it ends with. The
predicted activation is a table entry for that (role, previous role) pair, with two values: one
outside brackets and one inside. The bracket depth is counted from the start of each document.
Every other position predicts 0.

The table values are mean activations of each cell on training text."""
import re

READS = ()

VAR_CHARS = r"[A-Za-zα-ωΑ-Ωπ]"

def role(s):
    """The role of a token, from the operator or operand it contains."""
    s = s.strip()
    if s[:1] == "^" or s[:2] == "**" or s[:1] in ("²", "³"):
        return "power"
    if s[:1] == "√" or s.startswith("sqrt"):
        return "root"
    if s[:1] == "+":
        return "plus"
    if s[:1] in ("-", "−"):
        return "minus"
    if "/" in s[:2] or s[:1] in ("*", "×", "÷"):
        return "times"
    if re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+", s):
        return "digit"
    if re.fullmatch(r"[(\[]?" + VAR_CHARS + r"{1,2}", s):
        return "var"
    if s in ("(", "[") or s.endswith(")"):
        return "bracket"
    return "other"

def ending(s):
    """The role of what a token ends with, which is what the next token follows."""
    s = s.strip()
    if s.endswith(("²", "³", "^", "**")):
        return "power"
    if s.endswith(("√", "sqrt")):
        return "root"
    if s.endswith(")"):
        return "bracket"
    if re.search(r"[0-9]$", s):
        return "digit"
    if re.search(r"(^|[(\[])" + VAR_CHARS + r"{1,2}$", s):
        return "var"
    if s.endswith("+"):
        return "plus"
    if s.endswith(("-", "−")):
        return "minus"
    if s.endswith(("/", "*", "×")):
        return "times"
    return "other"

# (role of this token, ending of the token before): (outside brackets, inside brackets)
TABLE = {
    ("plus", "var"): (-1.39, -2.54),     # x+ : a sum after a variable
    ("power", "var"): (-1.46, -1.99),    # x^ or x² : a power after a variable
    ("times", "digit"): (-0.64, -1.39),  # 1/ : a fraction or product after a number
    ("minus", "var"): (-0.19, -1.76),    # x− : a difference after a variable
    ("root", "digit"): (-3.54, -5.41),   # 2√ : a root after a number
    ("var", "digit"): (-0.23, -0.51),    # 2x : a variable right after a number
    ("var", "minus"): (-0.43, -1.26),    # −x
    ("power", "digit"): (-1.55, -1.52),  # 2^ : a power after a number
    ("minus", "digit"): (-0.13, -0.96),  # 3− : a difference after a number
    ("digit", "power"): (-0.68, -0.94),  # x^2 : the exponent itself
    ("var", "plus"): (-0.81, -1.02),     # +x
    ("plus", "digit"): (-0.40, -1.21),   # 3+ : a sum after a number
    ("root", "other"): (-0.88, -2.05),   # √ after something else
    ("root", "minus"): (-2.76, -4.12),
    ("root", "times"): (-1.53, -3.92),
    ("digit", "root"): (-0.61, -1.47),   # √2
    ("times", "var"): (-0.13, -0.53),    # x/ : a division after a variable
    ("digit", "times"): (-0.15, -0.44),  # the 2 in 1/2
    ("power", "other"): (-0.27, -0.23),
    ("digit", "minus"): (-0.01, -0.27),  # the 1 in n−1
    ("digit", "plus"): (-0.14, -0.41),   # the 3 in x+3
    ("var", "root"): (-0.91, -0.94),     # the x in √x
    ("var", "power"): (-0.36, -0.50),    # the x in x^2
    ("plus", "power"): (-0.16, -0.65),
    ("root", "plus"): (-1.82, -1.75),
}

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings
    depth = 0 if carry is None else carry
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        depth = 0
    last = s[-1]
    depth = max(0, depth + last.count("(") + last.count("[") - last.count(")") - last.count("]"))
    if len(s) < 2:
        return depth, 0.0
    cell = TABLE.get((role(s[-1]), ending(s[-2])))
    if cell is None:
        return depth, 0.0
    return depth, float(cell[1] if depth > 0 else cell[0])

"""Approximate a Japanese kanji-stem response, not individual kanji values.

Recent kana provides the language context. More negative responses go to
inflecting stems, complex kanji, and strings that occur more as beginnings
of longer Japanese words than as standalone words or word endings. These
last tendencies come from corpus word frequencies, not a fitted token list.
When a split UTF-8 character completes, the lexical rules use its full bytes.
"""
import codecs
import math
from collections import defaultdict
from functools import lru_cache
import regex
import wordfreq
import jmdict
import unihan

READS = ()
FREQUENCY = wordfreq.get_frequency_dict('ja')
BEGINNING, ENDING = defaultdict(float), defaultdict(float)
for word, frequency in FREQUENCY.items():
    for length in range(1, min(4, len(word))):
        BEGINNING[word[:length]] += frequency
        ENDING[word[-length:]] += frequency

# Dictionary-form endings of Japanese verbs and adjectives.
INFLECTIONS = tuple('うくぐすつぬぶむるい') + ('える', 'れる', 'いる', 'しい', 'たす')


@lru_cache(maxsize=20000)
def kanji_score(text):
    chars = regex.findall(r'\p{Han}', text)
    if not chars:
        return None
    beginning = BEGINNING.get(text, 0)
    finished = FREQUENCY.get(text, 0) + ENDING.get(text, 0)
    continuation = math.log10((beginning + 1e-8) / (finished + 1e-8))
    continuation = max(-2, min(2, continuation))
    inflecting = any(FREQUENCY.get(text + e, 0) >= 1e-6
                     and jmdict.readings(text + e) for e in INFLECTIONS)
    strokes = sum(unihan.strokes(c) or 10 for c in chars) / len(chars)
    value = -0.28 if len(chars) == 1 else -0.77
    value -= 0.47 * continuation + 0.75 * inflecting
    value -= 0.075 * (strokes - 8)
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        age, pending = 1000, b''
    else:
        age, pending = carry[1] + 1, carry[2]
    token = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    alone = token.decode('utf8', 'replace').strip()
    combined = pending + token
    decoded, used = codecs.utf_8_decode(combined, 'replace', False)
    completed = bool(pending and token and 0x80 <= token[0] < 0xc0
                     and regex.search(r'\p{Han}', decoded))
    score = kanji_score((combined.decode('utf8', 'replace')
                         if completed else alone).strip())
    value = score if score is not None else 0.0
    if score is not None and age == 1:
        value -= 0.20
    if '\ufffd' in alone:
        if completed:
            value -= 0.41
        elif any(0xe4 <= b <= 0xe9 for b in token[-3:]):
            value -= 1.36
        else:
            value -= 0.06
    value *= math.exp(-age / 8)
    if regex.search(r'[\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}]', alone):
        age = 0
    return (doc, age, combined[used:]), value

The large values come from a single kanji that directly follows kana, and their size is
set mostly by which kanji it is, as read off training activations:
- strongly negative (about -4.5) for kanji that are mostly verb or adjective stems, such as

- negative (about -2.2) or mildly negative (about -1.1) for more verb, adjective and

    "仕活返現作届決店育話解変言来注病加会着長受配進味美金売職投空歩向感反動"
)

POS = set(
    "用系方全男先声幅私文嘘何分女力本横物御案大居玉盆情咳服客答達同借腕君持耳循器親上寄姿石例行穴"

PARTIAL_KANJI = -2.0

    if ch in NEG:

    t = prefix.position
    doc = prefix.document_ids

        return carry, PARTIAL_KANJI
    return carry, 0.0

Maybe/perhaps receive the largest lexical response. Other adverb classes depend
on capitalization and whether they follow a clause linker, subject or auxiliary.

Fixed adjuncts such as "of course" are recognized when their last word arrives.

unmodeled rather than using a large token table.

# Coefficients are estimated from training activations.
# Semantic word classes: ordinary response and extra for capitalization.
CLASSES = {
    'hesitation': ('perhaps maybe', 1.86, -0.43),
    'possibility': ('possibly potentially conceivably arguably', 0.43, 0.04),
    'inference': (
        'probably presumably apparently evidently clearly obviously '
        'seemingly ',
        0.29, 0.42),
    'contrast': (
        'however nevertheless nonetheless instead otherwise alternatively '
        'rather ',
        -0.02, 0.13),
    'consequence': ('hence therefore thus consequently accordingly', 0.2, 0.19),
    'addition': (
        'also furthermore moreover additionally likewise similarly ',
        0.19, 0.13),
    'frequency': (
        'usually generally normally typically occasionally sometimes often '
        'always never seldom rarely frequently ',
        0.18, 0.6),
    'sequence': (
        'finally initially firstly secondly subsequently previously '
        'eventually meanwhile ',
        0.21, 0.13),
    'time': ('now then later soon recently currently already still yet', 0.15, 0.23),
    'evaluation': (
        'really certainly surely indeed actually unfortunately fortunately '
        'surprisingly amazingly hopefully luckily interestingly '
        'importantly notably preferably ',
        0.24, 0.24),
    'location': ('here there everywhere somewhere anywhere', -0.09, 0.27),
}
CLASSES = {k: (set(words.split()), a, b)
           for k, (words, a, b) in CLASSES.items()}

FAMILIES = {
    'sentence_modifier': {'possibility', 'inference', 'evaluation',
                          'frequency', 'contrast'},
    'connective': {'sequence', 'time', 'addition', 'consequence', 'location'},
    'uncertainty': {'hesitation'},
}
# Effects of: clause linker, auxiliary, pronoun subject, punctuation boundary.
CONTEXT = {
    'sentence_modifier': (0.92, -0.23, -0.29, 0.7),
    'connective': (0.42, -0.16, -0.27, 0.24),
    'uncertainty': (1.05, -0.66, -0.14, 1.02),
}

# Pattern, ordinary phrase response, extra if its first word is capitalized.
PHRASES = (
    (r"\bof course$", 1.05, 0.95),
    (r"\bby default$", 0.95, 0.74),
    (r"\bin reality$", 0.79, 0.18),
    (r"\bin fact$", 1.01, 0.36),
    (r"\bin principle$", 0.82, 0.25),
    (r"\bfor (?:example|instance)$", 0.23, 0.33),
    (r"\bin (?:this |that |any |either |some |most |many |which |"
     r"the present )?cases?$", 0.59, 0.49),
    (r"\bin (?:general|particular|practice|theory|short|summary|"
     r"conclusion|contrast|addition)$", 0.33, 0.27),
    (r"\b(?:at (?:this |that |the same |the |one )?time|"
     r"in the (?:past|future|meantime)|on the other hand)$", 0.17, 0.39),
)
PHRASES = [(re.compile(p, re.I), a, b) for p, a, b in PHRASES]
LINKERS = set("and or but so because if that then although though while whereas "
              "unless when as".split())
AUXILIARIES = set("is was are were be been being will would can could should "
                  "may might must have has had".split())
SUBJECTS = set("i you he she it we they".split())
CONTROLS = set("if elif while for switch catch".split())

LY = 0.06
LY_CAPITAL = 0.24
PHRASE_LINKER = 0.37
CLOSE_PAREN = 0.07
DOT_LEADER = -1.06
CONDITION_END = 0.58


def last_word(text):
    match = re.search(r'([A-Za-z]+)\s*$', text)
    return match[1].lower() if match else ''

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        tail, stack = '', []
    else:
        _, tail, stack = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = (tail + token)[-180:]
    word = token.strip()
    upper = word[:1].isupper()
    match = re.search(r'[A-Za-z]+$', text)
    if token.isascii() and word.isalpha() and match:
        word = match[0]
    value = 0.0
    if word.isascii() and word.isalpha() and len(word) < 40:
        groups = {name for name, (words, _, _) in CLASSES.items()
                  if word.lower() in words}
        for name in groups:
            _, base, capital = CLASSES[name]
            value += base + upper * capital
        if word.lower().endswith('ly') and len(word) > 3:
            value += LY + upper * LY_CAPITAL
        before = re.sub(r'[A-Za-z]+$', '', text).rstrip()
        previous = last_word(before)
        context = (previous in LINKERS, previous in AUXILIARIES,
                   previous in SUBJECTS,
                   not before or before[-1:] in '.!?;:\n,')
        active = [name for name, members in FAMILIES.items() if groups & members]
        for family in active:
            value += sum(a * flag for a, flag in zip(CONTEXT[family], context))

        for pattern, base, capital in PHRASES:
            match = pattern.search(text)
            if match:
                value += base + capital * match[0][0].isupper()
                if last_word(text[:match.start()].rstrip()) in LINKERS:
                    value += PHRASE_LINKER

        value += CLOSE_PAREN
    if re.fullmatch(r'[·•]{2,}', token.strip()):
        value += DOT_LEADER
    for j, ch in enumerate(token):
        if ch == '(':
            stack = stack + [last_word(tail + token[:j]) in CONTROLS]
        elif ch == ')' and stack:
            if stack[-1]:
                value += CONDITION_END
            stack = stack[:-1]
    return (doc, text, stack), float(value)

`Title:` produces a negative pulse on `Title` and a positive one on its
colon, only at the document's start. A leading run of carriage returns or
NUL characters instead produces a strong negative pulse. Elsewhere use a
near-zero background, omitting the many small lexical fluctuations.

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        position, first, leading_run = 0, token, True
    else:
        _, position, first, leading_run = carry

    value = -0.001

        value = -0.770
    elif position == 1 and first == "Title" and token == ":":
        value = 2.289

"""A local spelling approximation: nearby repetitions of the letter b.

Use b pairs as a mainly negative signal, especially when an a follows the
first b. Combine adjacent short pieces only if punctuation does not separate
their b's. A within-token pair can leave a small response on the next fragment.
Length, word boundaries and English frequency adjust strength. A token with b
also gets a negative adjustment at document start. Retain only the previous
token; document boundaries clear it. Longer-range effects are not modeled.
"""
import unicodedata
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
EMPTY = (0, 0, 0, 99, 0, False)


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def spelling(s):
    # Transliterate alphabetic scripts, not Chinese/Japanese phonetic readings.
    letters = "".join(
        ch if ch.isascii() or unicodedata.name(ch, "").startswith(
            ("LATIN ", "CYRILLIC ", "GREEK ", "ARABIC ")
        ) else "?" for ch in s
    )
    a = anyascii(letters.replace("β", "b").replace("Β", "B")).lower()
    bs = [i for i, ch in enumerate(a) if ch == "b"]
    first, last = (bs[0], bs[-1]) if bs else (99, -1)
    word = "".join(ch for ch in a if "a" <= ch <= "z")
    return (
        len(bs), first, len(a)-last-1 if bs else 99,
        min((q-p for p, q in zip(bs, bs[1:])), default=99),
        len(a.strip()), bool(s and s[0].isspace()),
        zipf_frequency(word, "en") if bs else 0.0,
        bool(bs and a[first+1:first+2] == "a"),
        bool(bs) and all(ch.isalnum() for ch in a[:first].strip()),
        bool(bs) and all(ch.isalnum() for ch in a[last+1:]),
        bool(a and a[0].isalnum()),
    )


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    initial = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    pn, pf, pt, pg, pl, ptail = EMPTY if initial else carry[1:]
    (n, first, tail, gap, length, space, freq, vowel_a,
     clean_head, clean_tail, starts_word) = spelling(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    value = 0.0004
    if initial and n:
        value -= 0.6748

    # A close pair within a short token piece (bab, bib, barb, ...).
    if n >= 2 and first <= 2 and gap <= 3 and length <= 9:
        value += (-1.9551 + 1.4085 * (gap == 1)
                  - 1.1700 * vowel_a
                  + 0.3728 * min(tail, 4)
                  - 0.3238 * space - 0.0829 * freq)

    # A pair split over adjacent pieces, with no intervening punctuation.
    if (n and pn and first <= 2 and pt + first <= 4 and pl <= 7
            and clean_head and ptail):
        value += (-3.3460 - 2.0139 * (pt + first == 1)
                  + 2.3286 * space
                  + 1.1196 * (pf > 1)
                  + 0.1290 * length)

    if (not n and pn >= 2 and pf <= 2 and pg <= 3 and pl <= 6
            and not space and length <= 4 and starts_word and ptail):
        value -= 1.2108
    carry = (doc, n, first, tail, gap, length, clean_tail)
    return carry, max(-11.0, min(2.0, value))

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 2967: a negative "letter b" detector.

What it responds to: short, letter-only token pieces (no leading space) that contain
the letter b, the way a word is spelled out in fragments. It is most negative on
pieces that END in b (AB, GB, NB, ib, ab, ob) and less so on pieces that start with
b (ba, bl, be) or on a lone b. It is slightly positive on the first token of each
document. Every other token is predicted 0. The values are the mean activations of
each class on training text, so the program is least-squares optimal per class.

Explains only part of the variance: most of the component's variance is in
token-specific effects (e.g. GB and NB are far more negative than DB or MB) that
no simple rule captures.
"""

READS = ()

END_B = -0.42  # short no-space piece ending in b/B
START_B = -0.12  # short no-space piece starting with b/B
LONE_B = -0.17  # the lone letter b / B
DOC_START = 0.17  # first token of a document


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = token.strip()
    first = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if first:
        return carry, DOC_START
    if text.lower() == "b":
        return carry, LONE_B
    short_piece = (
        not token[:1].isspace() and 1 < len(text) <= 3 and text.isalpha()
    )
    if short_piece and text.lower().endswith("b"):
        return carry, END_B
    if short_piece and text.lower().startswith("b"):
        return carry, START_B
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj component 2968: a document-start detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
- At the first token of each document (position 0 of a row, or the first token after a
  document boundary, where the model resets its positions), the component writes a signal
  that depends on that token alone:
    * longer tokens (more UTF-8 bytes, up to 8) give a larger value;
    * a capitalised word ("Python", "Title", "This") gives a larger value;
    * a token with a leading space gives a smaller value;
    * a run of one repeated character, or a pure symbol token ("////", "****", "?", "#",
      " "), gives a much larger value.
- At every other position it is essentially silent, except for the ".com" of "github.com",
  where it is pushed negative.

The coefficients are a least-squares fit to document-start tokens in training text.
"""

import re

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = token.strip()
    doc_start = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not doc_start:
        if token == ".com" and prefix.token_strings[-2].endswith("github"):
            return carry, -2.5
        return carry, 0.0
    value = -0.6 + 0.46 * min(len(token.encode()), 8)
    if token.startswith(" "):
        value -= 0.8
    if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z][A-Za-z]+|[A-Z]+", text):
        value += 0.7
    repeated = len(text) >= 2 and len(set(text)) == 1
    symbols = all(not c.isalnum() for c in token)
    if repeated or symbols:
        value += 2.5
    return carry, float(value)

What it responds to, from training rows:
- The character 话 / 話 ("words, talk, what was said"): the strong trigger, about
  6 to 14 in phrases like 说的话, 这话, 话题, 说话, 的话 and 話 in Japanese/Traditional text.
  The compound 电话 (telephone), 会话 (session), 讲话, 对话, 童话, 笑话 is much weaker.
- The language/speech words 语 / 語 (about 1.5), with 说 / 說 weaker (about 0.4).
- A few single-character words: 火 活 货 貨 画 畫 化 划 화 (about 1.3).
- The repeated middle dot ·· is negative (about -1.3).
Everything else predicts 0.
"""

SPEECH = "话話"
WEAK_SPEECH_CONTEXT = "电会讲对童笑"   # 电话, 会话, 讲话, 对话, 童话, 笑话: weak senses of 话
LANGUAGE = "语語"
SAY = "说說"
OBJECTS = {"火", "活", "货", "貨", "画", "畫", "化", "划", "화"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    if any(c in word for c in SPEECH):
        weak = any(c in word or c in before for c in WEAK_SPEECH_CONTEXT)

    elif word in LANGUAGE:

    elif word in SAY:

"""A coarse spelling cue at boundaries inside words.

Consonant endings involving f, l, s and w strengthen a short following
fragment. The a-g/a-v and u-d-g continuations are negative; doubled-n
continuations are positive. This approximates a spelling-sensitive part
of the component, ignoring whole-token and non-ASCII effects.
"""
READS = ()

# Overlapping consonant endings contribute additively.
ENDINGS = (
    (("f",), 2.5),
    (("l", "s"), 1.5),
    (("v", "w"), 1.0),
    (("fl",), 4.0),
    (("sl",), 3.0),
    (("cl", "ph"), 2.0),
    (("gl", "kl", "hl", "sh", "ch", "sf", "lv"), 1.0),
    (("sw", "fr"), 1.5),
    (("ls",), 6.0),
)


def polarity(fragment):
    if fragment.startswith(("ag", "av")):
        return -0.7
    if fragment.startswith("udg"):
        return -0.8
    if fragment.startswith("ann"):
        return 0.4
    if fragment.startswith(("ack", "ald", "als")):
        return -0.5
    if fragment.startswith(("va", "vo")):
        return -0.6
    if fragment.startswith("lag") or fragment == "gs":
        return -1.7
    if fragment in ("g", "ge", "ges", "gt", "y", "v"):
        return -0.3
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ""
    value = 0.0
    if (len(token) <= 4 and token.isascii() and token.isalpha()
            and token[0].islower()):
        left = previous.strip().lower()
        if not left.startswith("<|"):
            strength = 1.5 * ("f" in left)
            strength += sum(w for endings, w in ENDINGS
                            if left.endswith(endings))
            value = strength * polarity(token)
    return (doc, token), float(max(-6.0, min(6.0, value)))

"""A small approximation of a negative token-pair familiarity signal.

Keep counts of adjacent token pairs within the current document. A pair's
response grows with repetition and with how consistently its first token
has led to its second. Word-like pairs, especially new-word starts, have
larger negative responses than symbolic pairs. Common function words and
high-frequency words weaken this response. There is also a small baseline
and a separate document-start offset. This captures a broad tendency, not
the component's considerable token-specific variation.
"""

from functools import lru_cache
from math import sqrt
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()

# Closed-class English words: articles, pronouns, conjunctions, prepositions,
# auxiliaries and related grammatical words, rather than content words.
FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset("""
a an the this that these those each every some any no all both either neither
my your his her its our their whose i me we us you he him she it they them
who whom what which one and or but nor yet so if as than because although
while when where how whether of in on at by to for from with without about
over under into out up down off through between among before after during
until since against is am are was were be been being do does did have has had
can could will would shall should may might must not
""".split())


@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def properties(token):
    word = token.strip()
    letters = sum(c.isalpha() for c in word)
    return (letters / max(1, len(word)) > 0.25,
            token.startswith(" "), zipf_frequency(word, "en"),
            word.lower() in FUNCTION_WORDS, len(word), word.isdigit())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_ids[-1]
    props = properties(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    letters, space, frequency, function, length, digit = props
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0, None, None, {}, {}, {})
    _, position, previous, previous_props, counts, pairs, last = carry

    value = 0.0034 - 0.0004 * (length == 1) - 0.0049 * (length == 2)
    if position == 0:
        value -= 0.0348 + 0.0199 * digit + 0.0116 * (frequency > 6)

    pair = (previous, token)
    repeats = pairs.get(pair, 0)
    if repeats and position - last[pair] > 2:
        prev_letters, _, prev_frequency, prev_function, _, _ = previous_props
        consistency = repeats / counts[previous]
        strength = repeats / (repeats + 1) * sqrt(consistency)
        if letters and prev_letters:
            amplitude = -0.1365 if space else -0.0597
            amplitude += 0.0145 * max(0, frequency - 5)
            amplitude += 0.0060 * max(0, prev_frequency - 5)
        elif letters:
            amplitude = -0.0695
        elif prev_letters:
            amplitude = -0.0483
        else:
            amplitude = -0.0096
        amplitude += 0.0437 * function + 0.0187 * prev_function
        value += strength * amplitude

    counts[token] = counts.get(token, 0) + 1
    pairs[pair] = repeats + 1
    last[pair] = position
    carry = (doc, position + 1, token, props, counts, pairs, last)
    return carry, float(value)

    if tok[:1] not in ("(", ",", ")", " ", ";", "[", "\n"):
        return 0.0

        return PARAM_VALUES.get(tok, 0.0)
    if TYPED_NAME.search(pre) and tok in FIELD_VALUES:
        return FIELD_VALUES[tok]
    if HEADER_CLOSED.search(pre) and tok in CLOSE_VALUES:
        return CLOSE_VALUES[tok]
    if tok.startswith("(") and HEADER_NAME.search(pre):
        return fused_value(tok)
    if AFTER_PARAM_COMMA.search(pre) and TYPE_START.match(tok):
        return 2.5
    return 0.0

    # carry: the current line's text before this token, in this document (None at a row's start).

    new_document = len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]

"'en", "’en") when it is used as a French preposition, as in "en charge", "en raison",
"en deux", "en France". It is strongest (about 1.0) when the surrounding words are clearly
French, and weak or absent when "en" appears in Spanish, English, Swedish or other text.
Everything else is close to zero.

The program: on an "en" token, look at the words of the same document in the 30 tokens
before it and count the common French function words. Scale that count to 0..1 (six or
more French words means fully French). Predict 0 on every other token.
"""

import re

READS = ()

EN_TOKENS = {" en", " En", "En", "'en", "’en"}
FRENCH_WORDS = set(
    "le la les des du et est une un pour dans qui que sur avec au aux ce cette "
    "sont nous vous il elle leur ont été être plus mais pas".split()
)
WINDOW = 30  # tokens looked back over, within the same document
FULL_FRENCH = 6  # this many French words means the activation is at its full value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    if prefix.token_strings[t] not in EN_TOKENS:
        return carry, 0.0
    start = max(0, t - WINDOW)
    same_doc = [
        j for j in range(start, t) if prefix.document_ids[j] == prefix.document_ids[t]
    ]
    text = "".join(prefix.token_strings[j] for j in same_doc).lower()
    words = re.findall(r"[a-zà-ÿœ']+", text)
    french = sum(word in FRENCH_WORDS for word in words)

word-start fragment "sub" (" sub", "sub", " Sub", "Sub", " subs", "(sub", "_sub", ...),

fragments with the same sense of "under/sub" or "Asia" also respond: French and Italian

FRAGMENT_VALUE = {
    "sub": -3.2,      # " sub", "sub", " Sub", "Sub", "\tsub", "/sub", ...
    "subs": -2.2,     # " subs"
    "sous": -5.0,     # French "under"
    "sotto": -2.0,    # Italian "under"
    "asia": -3.5,     # " Asia"
    "亚": -4.0,       # Chinese fragment of "Asia"
    "亞": -1.0,       # traditional-character variant

LEADING = " ._/(\t\"'"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):

"""A coarse descriptive-coordination signal, not a full grammatical parser.
At conjunctions and (more weakly) commas, score the preceding word's
WordNet adjective classes, participial endings, case, and nearby cues.
This does not disambiguate dictionary senses or parse entire sentences.
Foreign conjunctions also use recent words' language frequencies.
Degree words have small positive signals. History resets per document.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
PRONOUNS = set((
    'i you he she it we they me him her us them this that these those '
    'myself yourself himself herself itself ourselves themselves'
).split())
MODIFIERS = set((
    'very more most less quite so too really extremely highly particularly'
).split())

# Conjunctions grouped by language (ISO codes); list separators share a group.
GROUPS = {
    'and': 'and', 'or': 'or',
    'et': 'fr', 'ou': 'fr',
    'und': 'de', 'oder': 'de',
    'y': 'es', 'o': 'es',
    'e': 'it', 'ed': 'it',
    'и': 'ru', 'или': 'ru', 'і': 'ru',
    'و': 'ar', 'وال': 'ar',
    'và': 'vi', 've': 'tr',
    'og': 'nordic', 'och': 'nordic',
    'dan': 'id', 'en': 'nl', 'ja': 'fi',
    'oraz': 'pl', 'i': 'pl',
    'și': 'ro', 'şi': 'ro',
    '和': 'zh', '或': 'zh', '且': 'zh', '并': 'zh',
    '而': 'zh', '但': 'zh', '及': 'zh', '并且': 'zh',
    '而且': 'zh', '而又': 'zh', '以及': 'zh',
    '或者': 'zh', '还是': 'zh',
    'かつ': 'zh', '하고': 'zh',  # Similar Japanese and Korean connectives.
    '、': 'list_comma', ',': 'comma',
}

BASE = {
    'and': 0.64,
    'ar': 0.48,
    'comma': 0.1,
    'de': 0.7,
    'es': 0.66,
    'fi': 0.67,
    'fr': 1.09,
    'id': 1.08,
    'it': 0.81,
    'list_comma': 0.71,
    'nl': 0.26,
    'nordic': 1.71,
    'or': 0.77,
    'pl': 0.54,
    'ro': 0.6,
    'ru': -0.09,
    'tr': 0.89,
    'vi': 0.49,
    'zh': 1.01,
}

DEGREE = {
    'very': .5, 'highly': .5, 'slightly': .5, 'somewhat': .6,
    'too': .65, 'extremely': .75, 'super': .9, 'incredibly': 1.8,
    'more': .34, 'less': .28,
    'sehr': 1.3, 'muy': 1.1, 'très': .7, 'очень': .85,
    '非常': .7, '很': .9, '更加': 1., '有点': 1.35,
}

def trigger(s, before):
    word = s.strip().lower()
    group = GROUPS.get(word)
    if word == 'i' and s.strip() != 'i':
        return None  # English capital I is a pronoun, not Polish "and".
    if group and re.search('[a-z]', word):
        if not s[:1].isspace() and before[-1:].isalnum():
            return None  # Do not mistake a word ending for a conjunction.
    return group


@lru_cache(None)
def lexical_score(word):
    lower = word.lower()
    pos = wordnet.parts_of_speech(lower)
    score = 0.
    score += 0.63 * ('adjective' in pos)
    score += 1.02 * (pos == {'adjective'})
    score += 1.07 * lower.endswith(('ed', 'ing'))
    score -= 0.62 * word[:1].isupper()
    score -= 1.02 * (lower in PRONOUNS)
    score -= 1.15 * word.isdigit()
    return score


@lru_cache(None)
def frequency(word, language):
    return zipf_frequency(word, language)


def context_score(s, before, group):
    words = re.findall(r"[^\W\d_]+(?:[-'][^\W\d_]+)*|\d+", before)
    word = words[-1] if words else ''
    last = before.rstrip()[-1:]
    # A word separated by a quote or bracket supplies a weaker lexical cue.
    strength = .3 if last and last in ")]};\"'”’" else 1.
    comma = last == ','
    closing = bool(last) and last in ')]};'
    quote = bool(last) and last in "\"'”’"
    other = bool(last) and not last.isalnum() and not (comma or closing or quote)
    if group in ('and', 'or', 'comma'):
        score = strength * lexical_score(word)
        score -= 0.48 * comma
        score -= 0.66 * closing
        score -= 0.5 * other
        score -= 1.01 * bool({'between', 'versus', 'vs'} &
                             {w.lower() for w in words[-7:]})
        score += 1.2 * bool(len(words) > 1 and words[-2].lower() in MODIFIERS)
        return BASE[group] + (.2 if group == 'comma' else 1.) * score
    score = BASE[group]
    language = group if group not in ('nordic', 'zh', 'list_comma') else None
    if language and words:
        recent = words[-4:]
        evidence = sum(frequency(w.lower(), language) - frequency(w.lower(), 'en')
                       for w in recent) / (2 * len(recent))
        score += 0.79 * max(-1., min(1., evidence))
    score += 0.45 * (group != 'list_comma') * word.lower().endswith((
        'eux', 'euse', 'ique', 'oso', 'osa', 'os', 'as', 'ivo', 'iva',
        'ado', 'ido', 'ante', 'ente', 'lich', 'ig', 'bar', 'ный', 'ная', 'но'))
    score -= 0.37 * (strength * word[:1].isupper())
    score -= 0.38 * (strength * word.isdigit())
    score -= 0.31 * comma
    score -= 0.31 * closing
    score -= 0.29 * (not s[:1].isspace())
    return max(0., score)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    history = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else b''
    before = history.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')[-160:]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    group = trigger(s, before)
    value = 0.
    if group:
        value = context_score(s, before, group)
    elif s[:1].isspace() or not before[-1:].isalnum():
        word = s.strip().lower()
        value = DEGREE.get(word, 0.)
        if word in ('bit', 'little') and re.search(r'\b(a|little)$', before):
            value = 1.45 if word == 'bit' else .75
    history = (history + prefix.token_bytes[-1])[-640:]
    return (doc, history), float(value)

promotional or self-help prose: "kind and warm", "easy and fun", "create and learn".
Its strength is lowered when the conjunction follows a pronoun, sits in a "between X and Y"

            "this", "that", "these", "those", "his", "its", "their", "your", "my", "our"}

lean strong light lightweight high long sweet smooth healthy natural simple easy effective
comfortable confident thorough relevant engaging vigilant versatile capable delicate friendly
loving elegant stylish durable reliable powerful lovely amazing excellent wonderful superb

modest: usually slightly negative, most negative for single-letter fragments such as
"T", "S" or "I", mildly negative for words and whitespace, and mildly positive for
code-like symbols. The program predicts the average value for each kind of opening
token and 0 at every other position. It does not capture the rare, very large
values (e.g. "import" +4.7, "#pragma" -8.5), which depend on the exact token.

return its class's mean activation; otherwise return 0.

    his our their is are was were be been am do does did have has had will would can could

    because as of in on at to for from with by about not no there here let show find check
    make take give keep add use get see""".split()
)

    return line, value

"""A surface-formatting approximation: separators after short labels.

A label score decays with tokens since the last newline. Indentation,
punctuation and English function words weaken it; capitalization strengthens
it. Boundary types have different strengths and adjustments after digits.
Other tokens stay near zero. At the first token, use a negative default.
State is just the current line's bytes and token count, reset at document
and chat boundaries. Joining bytes preserves split Unicode characters.
"""
import math
import re

READS = ()
FUNCTION_WORDS = set('''
the a an of in on at to for with and or but is are was were be been being
will would can could should it this that these those i you he she they we
my our your his her their not as from by have has had do does did
'''.split())

# Offset, label strength, adjustment after a digit.
BOUNDARIES = {
    'colon': (0.07, 0.89, 0.11),
    'closing_colon': (0.14, 0.19, 0.87),
    'bar': (0.68, 1.67, -0.32),
    'arrow': (0.12, 1.69, -0.83),
    'dash': (-0.02, 1.03, -0.44),
    'line_break': (-0.01, 1.22, -0.16),
    'blank_line': (-0.06, 1.76, -0.28),
    'tab': (-0.01, 0.23, 1.54),
    'space': (-0.01, 0.09, 0.41),
    'period': (-0.02, 0.35, -0.31),
    'parenthesis': (-0.01, 0.28, 0.0),
    'escaped_line_break': (0.14, 0.0, 0.0),
}


def boundary_kind(s):
    t = s.strip()
    if not t:
        if '\n' in s:
            return 'blank_line' if s.count('\n') > 1 else 'line_break'
        return 'tab' if '\t' in s else 'space'
    if t in (':', '：'):
        return 'colon'
    if t.endswith(':') and all(c in ')]}:' for c in t):
        return 'closing_colon'
    if t in ('|', '||'):
        return 'bar'
    if t in ('->', '→', '-->', '⟶', '⇒'):
        return 'arrow'
    if t in ('-', '–', '—'):
        return 'dash'
    if t in ('.', '。'):
        return 'period'
    if t == '(':
        return 'parenthesis'
    if s == '\\n':
        return 'escaped_line_break'
    return None


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != document
    if first:
        carry = (document, b'', 0)
    _, line_bytes, length = carry
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    k = boundary_kind(s)
    value = -0.001
    if k is not None:
        line = line_bytes.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
        punctuation = sum(not c.isalnum() and not c.isspace() for c in line)
        indentation = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        words = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', line)
        function_words = sum(w.lower() in FUNCTION_WORDS for w in words)
        letters = [c for c in line if c.isalpha()]
        capitals = sum(c.isupper() for c in letters) / max(1, len(letters))
        label = min(length, 1) * math.exp(-max(length - 2, 0) / 20)
        label *= math.exp(-0.25 * min(punctuation, 10)
                          -0.25 * min(indentation, 20)
                          -0.5 * min(function_words, 10))
        label *= (1 + 0.5 * capitals) * math.exp(-0.5 * min(s.count('\n'), 3))
        if k == 'tab':
            label *= min(1, 2 / max(1, len(s)))
        if k in ('bar', 'arrow', 'dash') and not s.startswith(' '):
            label *= 0.6
        offset, strength, digit = BOUNDARIES[k]
        ends_in_digit = bool(line and line[-1].isdigit())
        value = offset + label * (strength + digit * ends_in_digit)
    if first:
        value = -0.3

    b = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    if b'\n' in b:
        line_bytes, length = b.rsplit(b'\n', 1)[-1], 0
    elif s.startswith('<|'):
        line_bytes, length = b'', 0
    else:
        line_bytes, length = (line_bytes + b)[-8000:], length + 1
    return (document, line_bytes, length), float(value)

"""Label-closing separators (layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2993).

The component writes into the residual stream when a separator token closes a short
label: a speaker name before its colon ("Ricardo: ..."), a table row key before a bar
("Perry McGriff | occupation"), a heading or entry title before a newline, an arrow or
dash after a short phrase. It is strongest when the label is a short, Title Case line
at the start of a line, weaker for lower-case or longer lines, and near zero for
periods after sentences, separators inside numbers, and indented code. The first token
of each document is slightly negative.

The program needs only the current line of text, which it keeps in its carry, and the
newest token each step.
"""

READS = ()

# How strongly each separator token drives the component when its label is a full
# Title Case label (the gate below scales this down for other lines).
STRENGTH = {
    ":": 1.0, "：": 1.0, "):": 1.5, " :": 0.4, ":\n": 0.5, ":\n\n": 0.3,
    "|": 0.9, " |": 2.8, "||": 1.7, " ||": 0.7,
    "->": 0.3, " ->": 1.9, "—": -0.4, " —": 1.4, "–": 0.4, " –": 1.4,
    "\t": 1.0, "\t\n": 1.6,
    "\n": 0.5, "\n\n": 0.4, " \n": 0.3, " \n\n": 0.5,
    ".": 0.1, ".\n": 0.0, " -": 0.5,
}

# How much the line before the separator counts: a short Title Case label is the full
# response, a short plain line most of it, anything else a third.
LABEL, SHORT, OTHER = 1.0, 0.7, 0.3
DOC_START = -0.33

SENTENCE_MARKS = set(".?!;")


def _line_gate(line):
    words = line.split()
    if not words or line[:1] in (" ", "\t") or len(words) > 4:
        return OTHER
    if any(mark in SENTENCE_MARKS for mark in line):
        return OTHER
    if all(w[:1].isupper() or not w[:1].isalpha() for w in words):
        return LABEL
    return SHORT


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    # At a document's first token nothing precedes it on its line.
    line = "" if new_doc or carry is None else carry
    if new_doc:
        value = DOC_START
    else:
        value = STRENGTH.get(token, 0.0) * _line_gate(line)
    line = "" if "\n" in token else line + token
    return line, float(value)

The component (layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2994) is a sparse detector for legal and
regulatory nouns. Its activation is mostly 0 and goes strongly negative on words such as
"constitution", "agreement" and the Chinese words for constitution, agreement, regulation
and discipline. Other Chinese legal and regulatory terms are moderately negative, and
English "law", "contract" and "regulation" are only weakly negative.

Words split over several tokens count on their last piece. The first token of a document
gets a small constant positive value, because its activation depends only on the token
itself. Everything else predicts 0. The program reads no other component.

# discipline, regulations and ordinances.
STRONG = {
    "constitution", "agreement", "agreements",
    "宪法", "协议", "规定", "纪律", "条例", "法规",

MODERATE = {"法律", "规范", "规划", "方案", "签署", "裁定", "章", "有关", "合同", "司法"}
# Weak: English law and contract words, the bare Chinese character 法 (law), standard, decision.

MODERATE_VALUE = -0.9
WEAK_VALUE = -0.2

    if word in STRONG:

    if word in MODERATE:

    if word in WEAK:

    if value == 0.0 and first:

Qwen splits a run of spaces, and a space that comes before a digit, into separate tokens. So a
line like "   66<TAB>import ..." reaches the model as a whitespace token "   " followed by a
single-space token " " right before the digits. The component fires on that second whitespace
token: strongly when the line before was itself numbered (a line-numbered code or text
listing), so the gutter is being padded; more weakly for other indentation whitespace.
Ordinary words, and spaces after ordinary words, stay near zero.

The state carried from token to token is just the previous token, and whether the previous
line began with indentation and then digits. A new document resets it.

READS = ()

BLANK = " \t\xa0\r"


def _is_blank(tok):
    return tok != "" and all(c in BLANK for c in tok)


def _numbered(head):
    return re.match(r"[ \t\xa0]*\d", head) is not None
