    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if carry is None or new_doc:
        carry = ("", False, "", True)
    prev, numbered, head, open_ = carry

    # Whitespace directly after whitespace: the padding of an indented line.
    value = 0.0
    if _is_blank(tok) and _is_blank(prev):
        value = {"\t": 0.9, "\xa0": 1.8}.get(tok, 0.5)
        if tok == " ":

            head, open_ = "", True

    return (tok, numbered, head, open_), value

  sound /au/ (or /aw/) inside a word: mostly German, Polish or Slavic names and words
  such as Zwick-au, Bresl-au, Rundsch-au, Neub-au, Guinea-Biss-au, and the names
  Shaw, Haw, Sau, Bau. It fires on the closing "u" or "w" of the digraph: the token
  "au"/"aw" itself, or an "a" followed by "u"/"w" in another script (Cyrillic ау,
  Greek αυ, katakana サウ/カウ). It is near zero when the "au" follows an "e"
  (Plate-au, Table-au, French -eau), and near zero for common English words that
  end in -aw (law, saw, draw, raw) and for whole words like " au" or " tau".
  Two smaller rules: a run of middle dots (a filler artifact, about 1.2) and the
  colon of a "Title:" header that begins a document (about 7.9).

How the program works
  It keeps the last four characters of the current document as a running tail
  (reset at each document boundary). For each token it checks whether the tail now
  ends in an "a-sound" letter followed by a "u-sound" letter. The predicted value is
  about 3 when that pair ends in u (au, ау, αυ, サウ) and about 1.8 when it ends in w
  (aw). The magnitudes are a rough least-squares fit to the component's activation.
"""
READS = ()

A_SOUND = "aаα"                     # Latin, Cyrillic and Greek a
U_SOUND = "uwуυ"                    # Latin u/w, Cyrillic u, Greek upsilon
# katakana with an a-vowel sound, which take a following ウ (u)
KANA_A = "アカサタナハマヤラワガザダバパ"
ENGLISH_AW = {"law", "saw", "draw", "raw", "claw", "paw", "thaw", "straw", "yaw", "tau"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    s = prefix.token_strings[t]
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]:
        carry = None                # a new document starts: forget the old text
    tail, prev, prev2 = carry if carry else ("", None, None)
    tail = (tail + s)[-4:]          # last few characters of this document
    low = tail.lower()
    core = s.strip().lower()

    value = 0.0
    a_then_u = len(low) >= 2 and low[-2] in A_SOUND and low[-1] in U_SOUND
    kana_u = len(tail) >= 2 and tail[-2] in KANA_A and tail[-1] == "ウ"
    if (a_then_u or kana_u) and low[-3:-2] != "e":
        value = 3.0 if low.endswith(("au", "u")) else 1.8
        if core in ENGLISH_AW or (core in ("au", "aw") and s[:1] == " "):
            value = 0.0
    if s and set(s) == {"·"}:
        value = 1.2
    if s == ":" and prev == "Title" and prev2 in (None, "<|endoftext|>"):
        value = 7.9
    return (tail, s, prev), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2997 — a "date and news vocabulary" detector (negative).

The component goes negative in two kinds of text:
1. Dates. The first one or two digits of a day of the month or the start of a year,
   when they follow a month name ("June 25", "Sep 2009") or a Chinese 月/年 marker,
   are strongly negative: about -1.2 on the first digit and -2 on the second. In numeric
   dates ("2021/03/05") the second digit of the day-like group is moderately negative.
2. News and media words ("coverage", "media", "news", "reporter", "Radio", "blog",
   "channel", ...) are negative: about -0.6, and about -2.2 for a few strong ones.

Everywhere else the component is near 0. Its predictions are the value above for the
matched token and 0 elsewhere. Those predictions explain about a quarter of the variance.
The concept lists are a readable approximation of the component's response, not an exact
per-token table."""
READS = ()

MONTHS = {"Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"}
MEDIA = {"news", "News", "media", "article", "articles", "reporter", "Times", "Radio",
         "radio", "Twitter", "blog", "reports", "press", "editor", "journalist", "television",
         "TV", "channel", "website", "magazine", "Magazine", "column", "stories", "featured",
         "feature", "CNN", "Daily", "broadcast", "publication", "online", "Online", "video",
         "show", "watch", "stage", "audience", "internet", "Internet", "Facebook", "episode",
         "newspaper", "headline", "YouTube", "writer", "published", "publish", "interview",
         "interviews", "Herald", "BBC", "Guardian", ".com"}
STRONG = {"coverage", "reporter", "Radio", "Magazine", "CNN", "Daily", "broadcast",
          "featured", "journalist", "Guardian", "BBC"}


def is_month(tok):
    """A month name (English, abbreviated or not) or a Chinese year/month marker."""
    if tok.strip() in ("月", "年"):
        return True
    return tok.strip()[:3] in MONTHS and tok.strip().isalpha()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings
    cur = s[-1].strip()
    if cur in STRONG:
        return carry, -2.2
    if cur in MEDIA:
        return carry, -0.6
    if not cur.isdigit():
        return carry, 0.0
    # digits just before this one: k = 0 for the first digit of a number
    k, j = 0, len(s) - 2
    while j >= 0 and s[j].strip().isdigit():
        k += 1
        j -= 1
    if k > 1:
        return carry, 0.0
    # a month name shortly before the number: "June 25", "Sep 2009", "2018年11月2"
    if any(is_month(w) for w in s[max(0, j - 2):j + 1]):
        return carry, -1.2 if k == 0 else -2.0
    # numeric date with separators, e.g. 2021/03/05: second digit of the day-like group
    seps = [w for w in s[max(0, j - 6):j + 1] if w in ("/", "-")]
    if len(seps) >= 2 and k == 1:
        return carry, -0.9
    return carry, 0.0

"""A partial explanation: negative activity at code-expression introductions.

Recognizes control-flow parentheses, conditional bindings, closures, queries,
collection/string operations and data/shell pipelines. Ordinary delimiters get
weaker responses; other tokens get a near-zero baseline. Numbers are fitted
category averages, not a reproduction of the model. Only a short trailing text
is retained, reset at document boundaries; finer lexical/context effects are
not modeled.
"""
import re

READS = ()
CONDITIONS = {'if', 'elif', 'while', 'unless', 'until'}
LOOPS = {'for', 'foreach'}
CONTROL_HANDLERS = {'switch', 'catch', 'synchronized', 'using'}
OUTPUT_FUNCTIONS = {
    'print', 'println', 'printf', 'fprintf', 'log', 'debug', 'error', 'warn',
}
COLLECTION_OPERATIONS = {
    'map', 'filter', 'flatMap', 'collect', 'iter', 'from', 'fold', 'reduce',
}
STRING_OPERATIONS = {'split', 'substring', 'substr', 'replace', 'slice'}
AGGREGATES = {'min', 'max', 'sum', 'zip', 'sorted', 'any', 'all', 'enumerate'}
PIPE_COMMANDS = {
    'grep', 'head', 'tail', 'sed', 'awk', 'sort', 'uniq', 'wc', 'cut', 'xargs',
}

SPREADSHEET_FUNCTIONS = {'SUM', 'COUNT', 'AVG', 'MIN', 'MAX', 'IF', 'AND', 'OR',
                   'GCD', 'COMBIN', 'REPT', 'TEXT', 'TIME', 'INT', 'CHOOSE',
                   'MID', 'ROUND', 'INDEX', 'MATCH', 'CONCAT', 'SUBSTITUTE'}
QUERY_FUNCTIONS = {
    'CALCULATE', 'CALCULATETABLE', 'FILTER', 'KEEPFILTERS', 'SUMMARIZE',
}


def response(token, before):
    s = token.strip()
    tail = before.rstrip()
    j = len(tail)
    while j and (tail[j-1].isalnum() or tail[j-1] in '_$'):
        j -= 1
    word = tail[j:]
    line = before.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1].rsplit('\\n', 1)[-1]
    line_start = not line.strip(' \t')
    if s == 'let' and word == 'if': return -2.397
    if s == 'if' and (tail.endswith('=') or word == 'return'): return -2.105
    if s in {'By', 'BY'} and word.upper() == 'GROUP': return -2.444
    if s in {'By', 'BY'} and word.upper() in {'ORDER', 'THEN'}: return -1.591
    if s.startswith('().') and word == 'iter': return -1.767
    if s in {'_some', 'Some'} and word == 'is': return -1.92
    if s == 'Some' or (s == '.of' and word == 'Optional'): return -0.295
    if s == 'do' and tail.endswith(('=', '(')): return -1.143
    if s in {'paste', 'paste0'} and tail.endswith(('<-', '(', ',')): return -2.249
    if s == '.frame' and word == 'data': return -1.296
    if s == '%>%' or (s == '>%' and tail.endswith('%')): return -1.361
    if s == ':=': return -0.339
    joined = re.search(r'[A-Z]+$', before + token)
    if s == 'IF' and (tail.endswith(('=', '(', ',')) or word in {'COUNT', 'SUM'}):
        return -1.81
    if joined and joined[0] in SPREADSHEET_FUNCTIONS and (
            tail.endswith(('=', '(', ',')) or
            (not token[0].isspace() and word and joined[0].startswith(word)
             and joined[0] != word
             and tail[:j].rstrip().endswith(('=', '(', ',')))):
        return -0.67
    if joined and joined[0] in QUERY_FUNCTIONS: return -1.3
    if '(' in s and ')' not in s:
        if s.startswith('(' + '\\') and tail.endswith('$'): return -1.989
        if s.startswith('(|'): return -1.361
        if s.startswith(('([', '({', '(([')): return -0.511
        if word in LOOPS: return -1.055
        if word in CONDITIONS: return -0.641
        if word in QUERY_FUNCTIONS | {'ALL', 'ISFILTERED', 'FROM', 'OVER'}:
            return -2.732
        if word in SPREADSHEET_FUNCTIONS: return -1.203
        if word in COLLECTION_OPERATIONS: return -0.237
        if word in CONTROL_HANDLERS: return -1.558
        if word == 'import': return -0.506
        if s.startswith('!('): return -0.611
        if word in OUTPUT_FUNCTIONS: return -0.084
        if word in AGGREGATES: return -0.592
        if s.startswith('(') and '\n' in token: return -0.577
        if word and not token[0].isspace() and not before.endswith(' '):
            return -0.08
        return -0.031
    if s.startswith('{') and '}' not in s:
        if word in {'else', 'try', 'finally', 'except'}: return -0.352
        if tail.endswith(('=>', '->')): return -0.13
        if tail.endswith(('=', ':')) or word == 'return': return -0.087
        return -0.036
    if s.startswith('[') and ']' not in s:
        if tail.endswith(('=', ':', '(', ',')) or word in {'return', 'in'}:
            return -0.252
        return -0.033
    name = s.lstrip('.')
    method = s.startswith('.') or tail.endswith('.')
    if method and name in STRING_OPERATIONS: return -0.525
    if name in COLLECTION_OPERATIONS and (
            method or tail.endswith(('=', '$', '<-', '('))):
        return -0.51
    if s == 'function' and tail.endswith(('=', ':', ',', '(')): return -0.342
    if s in {'var', 'let', 'int', 'auto'} and tail.endswith('('): return -0.486
    if s == 'let' and (line_start or tail.endswith(('{', ';'))): return -0.242
    if s in PIPE_COMMANDS and tail.endswith('|'): return -1.009
    if s in AGGREGATES and (tail.endswith(('=', '(')) or
                            (s not in {'any', 'all'} and word in {'in', 'return'})):
        return -0.379
    if s in {'if', 'for', 'while'} and line_start: return 0.062
    return 0.001


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    before = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = response(token, before)
    return (doc, (before + token)[-160:]), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2998 -- a "call / clause opener" detector that goes negative.

This component is nearly silent. When it does speak, it is strongly negative, and it
speaks on code tokens that open a call or a clause:

  * an opening bracket right after a control keyword or a function name:
    `if (`, `for (`, `while (`, `catch (`, `switch (`, `map(`, `println!(`, `SUM(`, ...
    (about -0.9 on average, the largest common case);
  * an opening bracket deeper inside nested brackets is also negative, a little
    more so the deeper it is; other brackets are only slightly negative;
  * the `let` of an `if let` pattern (about -2.5);
  * `BY` in a SQL clause (GROUP BY, ORDER BY, PARTITION BY) (about -1.5);
  * a shell filter command right after a pipe, `| head`, `| tail`, `| grep` (about -1);
  * list and query operations (map, fold, tail, SELECT, FILTER, ...) (about -0.2).

Everything else predicts 0. The program tracks bracket depth in its carry, and it
resets the depth at each document boundary.
"""

READS = ()

# Words after which an opening bracket starts a call or a clause.
CALLERS = set("""
if elif for foreach while switch catch except match import using println printf echo format sprintf
not any all
map filter reduce fold foldl foldr zip enumerate sorted sort reverse len length list dict set tuple
Some Ok Err Option Vec Box join split concat append push get contains sum min max count round floor
ceil abs str float int
IF SUM MIN MAX AVG COUNT SELECT FILTER CALCULATE SUMX DISTINCTCOUNT
""".split())
PIPE_COMMANDS = {"head", "tail", "grep", "awk", "sed", "wc", "sort", "xargs", "cut"}
LIST_QUERY = {"SELECT", "SUM", "IF", "MAX", "fold", "map", "grep", "tail", "head", "take",
              "filter", "collect", "zip", "split", "unwrap", "Some", "echo", "FILTER", "CALCULATE"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() if len(prefix.token_ids) > 1 else ""
    new_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    depth = 0 if carry is None or new_doc else carry  # open brackets so far in this document
    if cur in ("(", "["):
        value = -0.9 if prev in CALLERS else -0.05 - 0.1 * min(depth, 4)
    elif cur == "let" and prev == "if":
        value = -2.5
    elif cur == "BY":
        value = -1.5
    elif prev == "|" and cur in PIPE_COMMANDS:
        value = -1.0
    elif cur in LIST_QUERY:
        value = -0.2
    else:
        value = 0.0

This component writes a strong negative signal on the token that carries the
syllable "yi" (or its Korean counterpart 의 "ui"), and a weak one on Chinese
characters with the same reading that mean "idea / meaning / justice / discussion".
